policy_title: End Homelessness and Support Children in Care
stated: Labour will develop a new cross-government strategy, working with Mayors and Councils, to put Britain back on track to ending homelessness. They will also work with local government to support children in care through kinship, foster care, and adoption, strengthening regulation of the children’s social care sector. Improved data sharing across services, using a single unique identifier, will better support children and families.

source.quote: The last Labour government made huge strides in ending homelessness. Building on the lessons of our past, Labour will develop a new cross-government strategy, working with Mayors and Councils across the country, to put Britain back on track to ending homelessness. Every child should have a loving, secure home. Labour will work with local government to support children in care, including through kinship, foster care, and adoption, as well as strengthening regulation of the children’s social care sector. Sadly, too often we see families falling through the cracks of public services. Labour will improve data sharing across services, with a single unique identifier, to better support children and families.

bearing_set.reason: A cross-government homelessness strategy directly bears on social/affordable housing stock and security of tenure — homelessness is the most acute form of housing insecurity and any credible reduction requires real stock or support interventions.

Looked-after children are one of the worst-performing cohorts on educational attainment; policy targeting kinship/foster/adoption pathways, regulation of children's social care, and joined-up data sharing plausibly affects the attainment gap for this disadvantaged group.

Introducing a single unique identifier for cross-government data sharing is a concrete surveillance/privacy mechanism — it enables comprehensive state tracking of individuals across multiple services, with real implications for privacy and freedom from state data-gathering, even where the stated purpose is welfare.

Kinship care specifically keeps children within family and community networks rather than institutional care, with a direct mechanism for improving social belonging and trust for one of the most socially isolated vulnerable groups.

membership_note: Policy has two substantive strands — homelessness strategy and children's social care reform — each genuinely touching distinct fundamentals; the data-sharing element adds a non-negligible privacy bearing.
